absent: Per slab collection, location tracker allocation and release, and full location record layout beyond displayed fields.
General vmemmap range and address population, page table level allocation, block buffer allocation, alternate map rules, and weak override behavior.
Sparse section initialization, node association updates, and early usage buffer lifecycle.
Swap table primitives for fetch store count flag zero folio and shadow conversion, plus cluster list and control group helpers.
Swap readahead tuning policy, fault path integration, and backing read execution.
Working set recency test, non resident aging, vector accounting, generation sequence handling, and shadow packing details.
Slab cache node iteration macro and slab list ownership outside the shown locked walk.

findings.text: Slab allocation tracking is exposed through a debug filesystem file whose operations connect open, sequential read, seek and release to a sequential iteration engine; open builds a private location tracker for the cache named by the inode and release frees it.

Iteration state is the file offset mirrored into a tracker index; start records the requested offset, next advances it and stays valid through the final record, stop performs no work, and display renders the record addressed by the current index.

Each displayed location reports its occurrence count plus symbolic call site or an unavailable marker when absent, aggregate and per object waste when present, timing summarized as minimum alone or as minimum average maximum, process identifier as single value or range, processor and node affinity only on multi unit systems with non empty masks, optional stacked call chain when stack storage is configured, and a distinct empty message when no locations were collected at offset zero.

Opening the trace sizes a bitmap for objects per slab and a location array sized from one page, selects allocation or free tracking from the file auxiliary number, walks every cache node skipping empty nodes and feeding partial then full slabs into a per slab collector, then orders collected locations by descending count before freeing the bitmap.

If private tracker creation, bitmap allocation, or location array allocation fails the open path releases any already acquired private state and bitmap and reports resource exhaustion without scanning slabs.
Scanning of a cache node partial and full slab lists occurs under that node list lock with interrupts saved, released before moving to the next node, so list membership is stable during collection.

Base page population for a virtual mapping range is offered as an early boot interface that forwards its range node and alternate map to a more general range population helper with default frame selection and no special flags.

Tail page reuse for huge virtual mapping optimization keeps one cached tail page per zone per order above a minimum; lookup indexes by order offset, rejects orders below minimum or above folio maximum, allocates a single zeroed block once on miss and converts it to its page descriptor for later reuse.

Huge optimization population first establishes distinct mappings for an initial head sized span and then populates the remainder of the range by reusing the frame number of the cached tail page, failing with resource exhaustion if tail acquisition or head mapping fails.
Write protection for the optimization walks page by page over the tail span after the head and applies write protection to each kernel page table entry found through the kernel address mapping.

Huge page mapping population iterates the range in huge page aligned steps, ensures upper page table levels exist, installs a huge leaf when the entry is empty and a huge sized block is available, accepts already huge entries after verification, refuses fallback when an alternate map is supplied but allocation failed, otherwise descends to base page population for that step.
Population flag value for page reference handling equals one.

Sparse section metadata exists in two build dependent layouts: a dynamically pointed table of section pointers, or a statically sized two level root array aligned to avoid cross node cache line sharing.
Mapping from section number to node number exists in narrow and wide build dependent forms sized for the configured node count, each cache line aligned across the full section index space.
The highest present section number is tracked in a global counter and sparse early usage buffers with their end pointer are retained only for initialization.

Swap table mark width is two bits and minimum count width is two bits; presence of a zero indicator depends on whether remaining bits in a machine word after mark and frame widths exceed that minimum.
Swap cache frame number width is selected by configuration from possible physical memory width, configured physical memory width, or machine word width, each reduced by page shift.

Swap cluster capacity and order handling are configuration dependent: huge page aware builds use huge page entry count with order preserved, other builds use two hundred fifty six entries with order collapsed to zero.

Swap cluster descriptor contains a spin lock, usage count, flag byte, order byte, atomic table pointer for per slot entries, extension table for large counts, optional memory control group table, optional zero bitmap when the table lacks a zero flag, and a list node for cluster lists.

Cluster usability progresses through temporary off list, free, non full and fragmented states that remain allocatable up to the fragmented threshold, then transitions to full or discard with a distinct maximum sentinel.
The cluster spin lock serializes descriptor fields other than the list node together with the corresponding swap map elements for that cluster.
Swap address space lookup returns either the global swap address space or a null pointer depending on build configuration.

When swap cache support is disabled the folio duplication, release, synchronous read, cluster and fault readahead, synchronous swap in, readahead update, retry allocation, presence test, shadow fetch and cache replacement helpers collapse to trivial results indicating invalid argument, absence, or no operation.
Swap readahead cluster exponent defaults to a tunable with maximum thirty one, and swap readahead order ceiling equals five.
Swap address space operations provide a no operation dirty handler with optional migration support, and the global swap address space binds to those operations with readahead enabled by default.

Per virtual area readahead state packs page aligned fault address together with window and hit counters into one atomic word using half page shift derived fields, with helpers to extract each component and to compose a value, a global hit counter initialized to four, and a default value of four when no state was recorded.

Swap cache presence and shadow retrieval read the per cluster slot table entry and interpret it as folio backed or as encoded shadow value stripped of flag bits, returning null when the kind does not match.

Validation before adding to swap cache must run with the cluster lock held; it reports missing table or empty slot as not found, already cached slot as already exists, and mismatched multi slot range in cached state count zero marking or control group as busy, optionally returning prior shadow and control group identity.

Replacement rewrites each per page slot of the new folio range to point at the new frame while preserving prior flags, warns if any slot did not previously point at the old folio, and in debug builds additionally verifies non overlapping old range when orders differ; both folios must be locked swap cached with a valid entry.

Swap cache allocation aligns the target entry down to the folio span, prechecks availability without holding state, constrains allocation mask for higher orders, allocates by memory policy or by faulting address, revalidates under lock, marks locked and swap backed and inserts, then charges control groups and handles charge or deferred accounting failures by removal unlock and reference drops before accounting statistics and joining the least recently used list for later read.
Refault notification is an external entry that delegates to a generational handler when generational reclaim is enabled and otherwise executes the classic working set activation path.

Classic refault requires a locked folio, attributes a refault counter to the owning control group least recently used vector by file or anonymous kind, tests shadow recency with promotion recording, and on recent shadows marks active, ages non resident information, counts activation, and when previously working set marked restores working set status with an additional counter.

Generational refault decodes shadow into control group node token and prior working set flag under read copy update protection, ignores vectors that do not match the folio current vector, counts refaults, and on recent shadows derives history index tier and reference count to accumulate a refaulted histogram, restoring working set state or updating reference bits accordingly.

Recency decisions depend on shadow encoded sequence distance from the current maximum within a bounded generation window using file or anonymous eviction masks; stale or foreign shadows are treated as not recent and produce accounting without promotion.
Sparse and swap internal headers define single inclusion guards to prevent repeated inclusion.
